scenario: [IRET.12.2]: when an activation ends, every `logical` fact whose last justification it was is retracted, and a retraction that ends another activation withdraws that one's facts too, inside the first withdrawal. Rule `make` on Trig emits seventeen `logical` F facts, one more than an activation's inline justification list holds, so the first withdrawal walks an array of seventeen ids. Rule `chain` on F 1, the first of them, emits two `logical` G facts. Retracting Trig ends `make`'s activation; retracting F 1, the first id walked, ends `chain`'s activation, whose withdrawal runs nested and must not disturb the seventeen ids still being walked. Expect every derived fact gone: fact_count 0. A runtime whose nested withdrawal reuses the outer walk's buffer overwrites its next two ids with G's, finds those facts already gone, and skips F 2 and F 3, which stay with no justifier: fact_count 2. PATH PINNED: libds `withdraw_justification` (rete/terminal.c) over `ds_tms_withdraw`'s owned array above DS_TMS_INLINE; the Mercury runtime's `ds.engine.end_justifications`, which has no shared buffer.
rules_ds:
schema Trig scope logical:
    v: Int key

schema F scope logical:
    i: Int key

schema G scope logical:
    k: Int key

rule make:
    Trig
->
    emit F logical i: 1
    emit F logical i: 2
    emit F logical i: 3
    emit F logical i: 4
    emit F logical i: 5
    emit F logical i: 6
    emit F logical i: 7
    emit F logical i: 8
    emit F logical i: 9
    emit F logical i: 10
    emit F logical i: 11
    emit F logical i: 12
    emit F logical i: 13
    emit F logical i: 14
    emit F logical i: 15
    emit F logical i: 16
    emit F logical i: 17

rule chain:
    F f where f.i == 1
->
    emit G logical k: 1
    emit G logical k: 2
